core_obligations: Set up the square (proof lines 11508-11521): for U' in C' with image U = u(U') in C, consider the commutative square of ringed topoi (Sh(pt), O'(U')) -> (Sh(C'), O') over (Sh(pt), O(U)) -> (Sh(C), O), and identify the derived categories with D(O'(U')) and D(O(U)).

Compute the pullbacks (proof lines 11522-11530): pullback along the lower horizontal arrow sends K to RGamma(U, K), pullback along the left vertical arrow sends M to M tensor^L_{O(U)} O'(U'), and since both ways around the square agree by the same-chapter composition result, one gets RGamma(U', Lg^*K) = RGamma(U, K) tensor^L_{O(U)} O'(U').

Verify quasi-coherence of the pullback (proof lines 11531-11549): for a morphism f' : U' -> V' in C' with image f : U -> V in C, the displayed five-term chain using the observation for V' and V and the quasi-coherence of K shows RGamma(V', Lg^*K) tensor^L_{O'(V')} O'(U') = RGamma(U', Lg^*K), which is the condition for Lg^*K to lie in QC(O').
proof_roadmap: Reduce quasi-coherence to a condition over a single pair U' -> U in the two sites.
Build the commutative square of ringed topoi with the point categories at the corners.
Identify the four pullbacks and use commutativity of the square to compute RGamma of the pullback.
Use quasi-coherence of K to complete the chain that verifies the defining condition.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the derived pullback Lg^* along a morphism of ringed topoi carries quasi-coherent modules to quasi-coherent modules (statement lines 11500-11505). The proof sets up a commutative square of ringed topoi whose corners are the point categories rigged with the rings of sections O'(U') and O(U), identifies the four pullbacks explicitly, and uses commutativity of the square to compute RGamma(U', Lg^*K) as RGamma(U, K) tensor^L O'(U') (proof lines 11508-11530); the defining condition for quasi-coherence is then verified by a five-term chain in which quasi-coherence of K supplies the crucial middle step (proof lines 11531-11549). The non-formal content is the bookkeeping through the square together with the recognition of the two pullbacks. The claim is H2: one diagram chase, written out in full.
